correctness.rationale: The all-prime finite-field reduction classification counts exactly p(p-1)^2/2 quadratics with 0 roots, p(p-1) with one singular root, and p(p-1)^2/2 with two simple roots; the p=2 derivative-zero branch is checked explicitly. One-step Hensel lifting partitions every p^3 coefficient lift. The zero mod-p branch g=p h accounts for 0,p,2p,p^2 roots. Removing exactly one all-zero coefficient vector yields the generating polynomial over p^6-1 outcomes, even when p=2 causes exponent collisions. Independent pair-evaluation counting verifies E R^2=3-2/p before conditioning. Standalone exhaustive enumeration of p=2,3,5,7 verifies all coefficient triples and both moments. All asymptotic statements are for fixed k; rare p-root mass gives leading constant one for k>=3. The finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact five-mass distribution for uniformly random nonzero coefficient triples of degree at most two modulo p² is not stated by the most directly relevant primary sources. Simhi (arXiv:2610.29911v1) proves O_k(1+p^{k-2}) for moments in Lemma 3.4 and proves an order-p^{-2} rare singular event in Appendix Lemma A.2, but neither delivers the complete probability law, the exact conditional first two moments, or leading constant one for all fixed k≥3. Other random-p-adic polynomial works concern field roots or location distributions rather than modular root multiplicities. Searches using equivalent descriptions and high-moment asymptotics found no implication-dominating theorem. This is best-knowledge priority assessment, not a uniqueness proof; a hidden broad finite-ring polynomial law remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed exact finite-ring polynomial root-count theorem may cover the five-mass law after specialization.
Literature indexing and access are incomplete, and an unlocated general root-count result could imply the present exact formula.
The source results from Simhi are stronger globally, but they do not directly imply this exact local formula.

value.rationale: The exact local root count rho_g(p²) is part of the recently published Gaussian-mixture random-squarefree-polynomial model. Degree two is the first nonlinear natural case. The full distribution establishes the sharp exponent and constant in the published local high-moment estimate and identifies a singular-lifting mass of order p^-2. It exhibits an explicit discrepancy between weak convergence to equal point masses at 0 and 2 and the limiting second moment 3. This is an exact mathematically motivated local invariant, not an arbitrary tabulation or unsupported downstream claim.
